analysis.note: Morphologically viṣaya, masculine nominative plural; Śaṅkara takes the referent here as indriyāṇi, senses indicated/denoted by their objects.
Qualifies dehinaḥ; in Śaṅkara’s construal the ‘intake’ is the bringing-in of sense-objects.

verification.detail: compound stem nirāhāra as Pum/Sasthi/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Genitive singular, ‘of the embodied one’; Śaṅkara glosses dehinaḥ as dehavataḥ.
Indeclinable ‘excepting rasa’; Śaṅkara explains the rasa as rāga toward objects.

verification.detail: avyayībhāva; whole form not in kosha/MW as indeclinable

analysis.note: Here not ‘juice’ literally but rāga, subtle attachment/relish, per Śaṅkara.
‘Even’; sandhi in raso 'py asya reflects rasaḥ api asya.
Refers to the yati/dehin in Śaṅkara’s gloss.
Substantivized neuter accusative: the supreme reality, Brahman, as glossed by Śaṅkara.
Absolutive/gerund, ‘having seen’; Śaṅkara glosses it as upalabhya, realization.
Subject is rasaḥ; Śaṅkara takes the cessation to be the removal of the seed of object-cognition.

justifications.decision: Although the surface noun is viṣaya, Śaṅkara explicitly glosses the verse’s viṣayāḥ as indriyāṇi, ‘senses,’ qualified by viṣayopalakṣitāni and viṣaya-śabda-vācyāni. The translation therefore says ‘the senses—called by their objects.’
options_considered: the senses, indicated/denoted by their objects, withdraw
justifications.chosen: viṣayāḥ means the senses indicated or denoted by their objects, not simply external objects.

evidence.translation: ‘viṣayāḥ’: the senses, indicated by objects and denoted by the word ‘object’.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara does not leave nirāhāra at the literal level of food-fasting; he glosses it as anāhriyamāṇa-viṣayasya, ‘whose objects are not being brought in,’ and frames it as austerity that may occur even in a fool.
options_considered: one who is merely without food
one whose intake of sense-objects is withheld
justifications.chosen: nirāhārasya dehinaḥ is the embodied one whose sense-objects are not being brought in, especially one standing in harsh austerity.

evidence.quote: nirāhārasya anāhriyamāṇa-viṣayasya kaṣṭe tapasi sthitasya mūrkhasyāpi
evidence.translation: ‘of the nirāhāra’: of one whose objects are not being brought in, even of a fool standing in harsh austerity.

justifications.decision: The compound/indeclinable is governed by varjam, which Śaṅkara paraphrases with varjayitvā; the thing excepted is rasa understood as rāga toward objects.
justifications.chosen: rasa-varjam means ‘excepting the rasa,’ where rasa is attachment/relish toward objects.

evidence.quote: rasa-varjaṃ raso rāgo viṣayeṣu yas taṃ varjayitvā
evidence.translation: ‘rasa-varjam’: leaving aside that rasa which is attachment toward objects.
The word rasa is well known in the sense of attachment.

justifications.decision: The second rasaḥ is not a different literal ‘taste’; Śaṅkara continues the same sense, calling it rañjana-rūpa and sūkṣma, a subtle coloring/attachment belonging to this yati.
options_considered: even the physical sense of taste
even his subtle attachment or relish
justifications.chosen: raso 'py asya is ‘even his subtle attachment/relish.’

evidence.translation: Even that rasa, subtle and of the nature of coloring/attachment, of this yati.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara identifies param with paramārtha-tattva, brahman, and glosses dṛṣṭvā with upalabhya, adding the realization ‘aham eva tat’; the translation therefore uses ‘having seen/realized the supreme (Brahman).’
options_considered: after seeing a superior worldly object
having realized the supreme reality, Brahman
justifications.chosen: paraṃ dṛṣṭvā means having realized the supreme reality, Brahman, as ‘I am that.’

evidence.quote: paraṃ paramārtha-tattvaṃ brahma dṛṣṭvā upalabhya aham eva tat iti
evidence.translation: Having seen—realized—the supreme, the ultimate reality, Brahman, as ‘I myself am that.’

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara glosses the cessation as nirbījaṃ viṣaya-vijñānaṃ saṃpadyate, and explicitly denies the destruction of rasa in the absence of samyag-darśana.
options_considered: temporary withdrawal produced by austerity alone
cessation of subtle attachment through right realization
justifications.chosen: nivartate means that attachment ceases in the strong sense of becoming seedless; it is not destroyed without right vision.

evidence.quote: nivartate nirbījaṃ viṣaya-vijñānaṃ saṃpadyate ity arthaḥ
evidence.translation: ‘It ceases’: object-cognition becomes seedless—this is the meaning.
When right vision is absent, there is no cutting off of rasa.

translation:
The senses—called by the names of their objects—withdraw
from the embodied one whose objects are not taken in,
excepting the taste, the attachment.
But even his subtle attachment ceases
when he has seen the supreme, Brahman.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation would likely render viṣayāḥ as external ‘objects’; Śaṅkara instead takes them here as the senses indicated by their objects.
It might take nirāhārasya as simple food-fasting; Śaṅkara’s gloss makes it the withholding of sense-objects, even in severe austerity.
It might translate rasa as literal ‘taste’ or ‘juice’; Śaṅkara explicitly defines it as rāga, subtle attachment/relish.
It might miss that paraṃ dṛṣṭvā is realization of Brahman and that attachment is not uprooted without samyag-darśana.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 segmented rasa-varjam as rasa + varjam; I treat the printed hyphenated expression as one indeclinable compound, following Śaṅkara’s gloss taṃ varjayitvā in line 1.
ByT5 labels dṛṣṭvā as a converb; under the required schema it is represented as an avyaya absolutive from √dṛś, not as a finite tinanta.
mula: viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ | rasa-varjaṃ raso 'py asya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate
commentary_lines: yadyapi viṣayāḥ viṣayopalakṣitāni viṣaya-śabda-vācyāni indriyāṇi nirāhārasya anāhriyamāṇa-viṣayasya kaṣṭe tapasi sthitasya mūrkhasyāpi vinivartante dehino dehavataḥ rasa-varjaṃ raso rāgo viṣayeṣu yas taṃ varjayitvā |
rasa-śabdo rāge prasiddhaḥ, sva-rasena pravṛttaḥ rasikaḥ rasajñaḥ, ity ādi-darśanāt |
so 'pi raso rañjana-rūpaḥ sūkṣmo 'sya yateḥ paraṃ paramārtha-tattvaṃ brahma dṛṣṭvā upalabhya aham eva tat iti vartamānasya nivartate nirbījaṃ viṣaya-vijñānaṃ saṃpadyate ity arthaḥ |
tasmāt samyag-darśanātmikāyāḥ prajñāyāḥ sthairyaṃ kartavyam ity abhiprāyaḥ ||bhgs_2.59||
samyag-darśana-lakṣaṇa-prajñā-sthairyaṃ cikīrṣatā ādau indriyāṇi sva-vaśe sthāpayitavyāni, yasmāt tad-anavasthāpane doṣam āha ---
